# The gates

Every module that exposes a `check` function, with the reasoning it carries in its own docstring. This page is extracted from those modules, so a gate cannot be described here and absent there.

Each gate recomputes independently, fails closed when an input it depends on is missing, and reads the artifact actually being delivered rather than a fixture. Each has negative tests that must go red on a deliberately broken input: a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate, because it grants confidence nothing earned.

## `A-sanitize`

`persona_to_skill/collect/sanitize.py`

Corpus text is downloaded from third parties, so it is hostile input.

This runs at ingest rather than at a gate, and the difference matters. If
stored text is already clean, the fingerprint covers the clean version and G2
never sees the attack. A gate that merely detected the problem would be
reporting on something already loaded.

A second pass over the corpus directory exists anyway, because a file placed
there by hand never went through ingest. Depth, not redundancy.

WHAT IS REMOVED, and the first one is the reason this file exists:

  Bidirectional overrides (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069) reorder how text
  displays without changing the bytes. That is an attack aimed squarely at G2:
  the quote matches the source byte for byte, and a reader sees something else.
  A gate verifying bytes while a human reads glyphs is exactly the gap these
  characters open, and a prose corpus has no legitimate use for them; genuine
  right-to-left text works from its base direction.

  Zero-width space and the byte-order mark are invisible and can be inserted
  to break a match or to make two identical-looking strings differ.

  C0 and C1 controls other than tab and newline cannot appear in prose and can
  truncate or confuse downstream readers.

WHAT IS ONLY FLAGGED, because removing it would do damage:

  Zero-width joiner and non-joiner are load-bearing in emoji sequences and in
  several Indic scripts. Stripping them corrupts real text.

  Mixed-script words, narrowly: Cyrillic or Greek letters inside an otherwise
  Latin word, which is how a quote is forged to look identical. Latin mixed
  with CJK is flagged by nothing here, because it is ordinary ("iPhone 用戶").

  Instruction-shaped sentences. These cannot be filtered away and should not
  be: a transcript may legitimately contain somebody saying "ignore the
  previous instruction". The defence is structural rather than lexical, and it
  is stated in one line because it is the whole of it: CORPUS TEXT IS ONLY EVER
  QUOTED, NEVER FOLLOWED. The flag exists so a person can see what arrived.

## `B-contradictions`

`persona_to_skill/extract/contradictions.py`

A contradiction is the find, not the problem.

Corpora do not change their minds; people do. A practitioner who argued one
thing in 2021 and the opposite in 2024 has rarely reversed. Usually an unstated
condition changed, and recovering that condition is the most valuable thing in
a whole reconstruction, because it is a criterion the subject has never spelled
out anywhere. Nobody can quote it, because it was never said.

So the earlier design here was wrong. "Use the newest, and record what changed"
treats a contradiction as noise to be resolved, and resolving it discards the
only thing that was worth having. Every record now has to answer one question:
what condition makes both sides true.

Fail-closed, and this is the rule that matters. Where no condition can be
found, the record stays UNRESOLVED and ships as something worth digging into.
Picking the newer side is not an available outcome, because it looks like
progress and is actually a deletion.

One lesser benefit, kept because it is real: a reconstruction that knows what
its subject has abandoned will not quote them on it, which is the fastest way
such an adviser loses credibility.

## `B-profile`

`persona_to_skill/extract/profile.py`

Per seat, not one number.

A practitioner is usually distinctive in one or two seats and ordinary in the
rest. Someone who has watched a lot of things fail has a strong oppose seat.
Someone who knows which figures lie has a strong evidence seat. Their
decompose seat may be no better than anyone's. A single alignment figure
averages that away and tells the reader nothing about where to trust the
result.

So the profile is per seat, and it is computed the same way the holdout gate
computes anything: against a recorded baseline, where the baseline is the same
question answered with no reconstruction loaded. A seat is

    distinctive  the baseline gets its questions wrong and the reconstruction
                 gets them right. Judgement carried across here.
    generic      the baseline already answers them. The reconstruction may be
                 correct and is adding nothing: it may not claim this seat.
    unfilled     the corpus had nothing to put in it. Not a finding about the
                 person.

What that buys is the honest claim. Instead of "84% aligned", a reconstruction
says which seats it earned, and the skill it produces claims only those. A
reader who knows the oppose seat is distinctive and the synthesise seat is
generic knows exactly how much to lean on each, which no single score can tell
them.

## `B-seats`

`persona_to_skill/extract/seats.py`

The seats, and what each one owes.

What is extracted is not what the subject concluded. A cited conclusion is
still a conclusion, and an adviser who walks in and says "looks fine" is
useless whether or not the sentence carries a footnote. So the unit of
extraction is a seat in a deliberation, defined by what the subject does in it:
how they carve the problem up, what they argue against, what evidence they
demand before moving, which number they say decides it.

Three things this module enforces, each of them a decision about what the
output is for rather than a detail of its shape.

ADVERSARIAL BY DEFAULT. The first seat that takes a position is oppose;
decompose precedes it only because a problem has to be carved up before
anything can be objected to. The support seat exists and is never volunteered.
The dangerous user is not the one with no view; it is the one who already has
an answer, holding a reconstruction of somebody they admire, because agreement
in that voice does not read as flattery, it reads as confirmation.

AN UNFILLED SEAT IS NOT AN ABSENT TRAIT. A seat with nothing in it means the
corpus had nothing to say, not that the subject does not deliberate that way.
The two are reported differently, and conflating them would let a thin corpus
pass itself off as a finding about a person.

EVERY SEAT ENTRY IS A CLAIM. Entries carry a source and a quote, or are marked
as inference, which is exactly the shape G2 reconciles. The seats are therefore
not a separate honesty system; they feed the one that already exists.

## `B-sensitivity`

`persona_to_skill/extract/sensitivity.py`

Which number decides it, and roughly where the line sits.

Most hesitation is not disagreement. Someone stuck on a decision usually has
the arguments already and is missing a quantity, which is why a third opinion
changes nothing and one lookup changes everything.

That reframes what a practitioner is worth. Not their view, which is often
consensus and which a general model already holds. What they have is knowing,
for this class of decision, which single quantity decides it and roughly where
the line falls. That claim is bounded and checkable, unlike "thinks like X",
and it hands the user something they can act on alone.

It also fixes the default behaviour. When the deciding number is not in hand,
the honest output is "go and find this out", not advice. An impersonating
reconstruction gives advice there, because advice feels like helping.

A threshold has to contain a number. That is what puts this file under G2's
figure check: a threshold the corpus does not contain cannot be written down,
so the most valuable field is also the one hardest to invent.

## `G2-anchor`

`persona_to_skill/gates/anchor.py`

G2: source anchor reconciliation.

Every claim attributed to the subject must name a source and quote it, and the
quote must appear in that source verbatim.

This gate recomputes independently: it reopens the corpus file from disk and
searches for the quote itself. It does not consult whatever index, offset, or
confidence score the extraction stage produced, because confirming an extraction with
its own bookkeeping is the self-referential gate that always passes.

## `G1-consent`

`persona_to_skill/gates/consent.py`

G1: source tier and consent gate.

Runs before anything is read for content: it decides which material enters the
pipeline at all, so no later stage has to ask.

Scope-independent by design. Whether the result stays on your laptop or ships
to customers, T3 material is material you were not given, and T0 material needs
the record that says you were.

Fails closed in three ways that matter:
  * a source with no tier is not "probably fine", it is an error;
  * T0 with no consent record blocks, rather than being quietly downgraded;
  * an unreadable consent file blocks, rather than being treated as absent.

## `G3-disclosure`

`persona_to_skill/gates/disclosure.py`

G3: disclosure and impersonation.

The one gate that depends on output scope, because it is the only one about
informing a third party. It reads the generated skill text about to be
delivered, not a template, not a fixture.

PUBLISHED scope blocks on:
  * any instruction telling a model to be, act as, or speak as the subject;
  * a missing or incomplete disclosure block.

These encode the test courts actually apply. In the US the 2024-2026
digital-replica statutes reach voice and visual likeness, and first-person
impersonation is the text form nearest that line. In Taiwan the questions are
混淆誤認之虞 (likelihood of confusion) and 攀附知名度 (riding on someone's
reputation); a disclosure block and a non-impersonating voice address both.

PRIVATE scope requires no disclosure, since nobody is being informed, and
downgrades impersonation to a warning about effectiveness rather than law. See
contract.IMPERSONATION_RATIONALE_PRIVATE. A private builder who wants
impersonation anyway gets it; the tool states why it is a worse tool and
proceeds. Deciding that for them is not this gate's job.

## `G4-holdout`

`persona_to_skill/gates/holdout.py`

G4: holdout alignment, scored against a baseline.

The only gate that distinguishes a reconstruction from a costume.

Questions the subject has publicly answered are held back from extraction. The
built skill answers them; the answers are compared with what the subject
actually said. Alignment on held-back material is evidence the method
transferred. Alignment on material the skill was built from is evidence of
nothing, which is why items flagged as seen are excluded rather than scored.

That alone is not enough, and this is the heart of the gate. Most of what any
practitioner says out loud is consensus, so a reconstruction scores well on
those questions whether or not it learned anything. Pooling them with the rest
produces a flattering grade for an empty shell.

So each item carries a BASELINE observation: the same question answered with no
reconstruction loaded. Items split in two:

    consensus pool  the baseline already matches the subject. Reported, never
                    gated: no credit for an answer the default gets right.
    divergent pool  the baseline is wrong, so only judgement that actually
                    carried across can be right. The gate reads this pool.

Alignment therefore means "alignment where the default would have failed",
which is the lift over baseline measured directly rather than subtracted.

UNKNOWN is a first-class state throughout. An item with no recorded observation
is not a pass and not a failure: it leaves the denominator and is reported on
its own. Scoring it either way would invent the measurement: as a failure it
slanders a reconstruction for a thin question set, as a pass it flatters one
for a check that never ran.

Note that `bool` is a subclass of `int` in Python, so a JSON `true` would
satisfy a naive isinstance(x, int) check and then be summed as 1, inventing a
score this module promises never to estimate.

## `G5-interrogation`

`persona_to_skill/gates/interrogation.py`

G5: interrogation of the deliberation memo.

The traps this gate exists to catch all hide in fluent prose, which is why
catching them cannot be left to an alert reader:

  * an unsourced claim written as established fact;
  * a recommendation quietly resting on an assumption nobody verified;
  * a hedge ("should be", "usually", "應該是") standing where "I do not know"
    belongs.

Fluency is the camouflage. The more polished a memo reads, the more it needs
this pass.

The gate works off a fixed schema, and the fixedness is the point. People
deciding something look at what they already want to look at, so the fields
anyone would skip (key assumptions, main risks, what evidence is missing)
have to be made non-skippable. A blank field is visible; a field never asked
for is not.

Two kinds of leak are checked separately, because they are different faults:

  evasion  a field filled with "work it out yourself" phrasing. The judgement
           was dodged.
  hedging  a statement classified as fact while carrying language that means
           not-knowing. The remedy is reclassification, not deletion: a hedged
           statement is an inference or an unknown, and saying so is honest.

Every statement carries one of four classes, and each class owes something:
    FACT            a source, and no hedging
    INFERENCE       what it was derived from
    ASSUMPTION      a verification status
    RECOMMENDATION  the statements it rests on, named at the recommendation

## `B-reconcile`

`persona_to_skill/gates/reconcile.py`

B-reconcile: the figures in the deliverable against the computed ones.

Three places in a bundle state the same measurement, and until this gate
existed nothing compared them:

  * `holdout`, the observations G4 scores;
  * `holdout_by_seat`, the per-seat slices B-profile scores;
  * `disclosure.holdout_alignment`, free text that the rendered SKILL.md
    publishes under the label "Measured alignment where a model with no
    reconstruction answers wrongly".

A worked example in this repository shipped an archive whose holdout-report
said 100% over 5 divergent items while its SKILL.md disclosed 92% over 12,
and whose per-seat lists totalled fifteen observations against a global set
of twelve. Nine gates passed. Every one of those numbers reads as measured,
and a reader has no way to tell which is.

The per-seat lists are slices of one run: the eval manifest gives each item
exactly one seat, so the slices partition the whole. Comparing them as
multisets of (aligned, baseline_aligned) catches a list written twice without
demanding the two be in the same order, which would be a different claim.

Fails closed. A bundle with no holdout cannot be reconciled, and G4 already
refuses that case; saying nothing here would turn the absence into a pass.
